# gns3_snapshot (Action)

Creates a snapshot of a GNS3 project, or restores one by name. With `restore = false` (the default) it calls `POST /v2/projects/{project_id}/snapshots` with `name`. With `restore = true` it lists the project's snapshots, picks the one called `name` and calls `POST /v2/projects/{project_id}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/restore`; it fails when no snapshot or more than one snapshot has that name. The action changes no state and has no outputs.

Actions need Terraform 1.14 or later. Invoke it from a resource's `lifecycle { action_trigger { ... } }` block or with `terraform apply -invoke=action.gns3_snapshot.<name>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Actions need Terraform 1.14 or later.
resource "gns3_project" "lab" {
  name = "tf-example-snapshot"
}

data "gns3_template" "vpcs" {
  name = "VPCS"
}

resource "gns3_node" "pc1" {
  project_id  = gns3_project.lab.project_id
  template_id = data.gns3_template.vpcs.template_id
  name        = "PC1"

  # Take a snapshot called "baseline" once the node exists.
  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create]
      actions = [action.gns3_snapshot.baseline]
    }
  }
}

action "gns3_snapshot" "baseline" {
  config {
    project_id = gns3_project.lab.project_id
    name       = "baseline"
  }
}

# Roll the project back to "baseline". Run it on demand:
# terraform apply -invoke=action.gns3_snapshot.restore_baseline
action "gns3_snapshot" "restore_baseline" {
  config {
    project_id = gns3_project.lab.project_id
    name       = "baseline"
    restore    = true
  }
}
```

<!-- action schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Snapshot name. GNS3 does not require names to be unique, but a restore needs exactly one snapshot with this name.
- `project_id` (String) ID of the project to snapshot or restore.

### Optional

- `restore` (Boolean) `false` (default) creates a snapshot called `name`. `true` restores the existing snapshot called `name`, replacing the project's current topology. On GNS3 2.2.61 a restore leaves every node stopped (node IDs are kept); start them again with `gns3_start_nodes`.
